subject: Dedicated reservation options: cluster sizing & ramp schedule
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Gray <daniel.gray@pinewave.com>, Priya Reddy <priya.reddy@pinewave.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Mar 2028 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated reservation options: cluster sizing & ramp schedule

Hi Daniel / Priya,

Following our pilot conversation last week, attached is a concise set of reservation options tailored to PineWave's inference needs. High-level choices below — I included an estimated burn / runway and a suggested ramp cadence for each. See attachment: pinewave-reserve-options-v2.pdf.

Options (all GPU counts refer to A100-equivalent capacity):
- Pilot Sprint — 8 GPUs (min floor 4)
  - Use case: narrow model set for early internal experiments
  - Ramp: 2 weeks activation, monthly review
  - Pros: lowest up-front 
- Growth Tier — 32 GPUs (min floor 16)
  - Use case: sustained production traffic, mixed RT/batch workloads
  - Ramp: month 1 = 16 (warm), month 2 = 24, month 3 = 32
  - Includes: warm-start credits, weekend burst windows
- Enterprise Slate — 96 GPUs (min floor 64)
  - Use case: full model fleet, strict latency SLOs, high throughput
  - Ramp: staged quarterly activation, dedicated on-call

Questions I have for you so we can finalize a proposal:
1) Do you have a preferred starting option or an absolute budget cap for Q2?
2) Any compliance or segregation needs (VPC/on-prem) beyond SOC2 that would affect pricing?
3) Would you prefer a monthly activation cadence or an aggressive 30/60/90 ramp?

If helpful, I can sketch a 3-month burn model for Growth Tier (32 GPUs) with warm-start credits and fallback to hosted instances to reduce risk.

Next steps: let me know which option to lock and any non-negotiables; I can turn this into a formal commitment deck and a draft SOW.

Thanks,
Markus Klein
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0182

Attachment: pinewave-reserve-options-v2.pdf (12 pages)

From: Daniel Gray <daniel.gray@pinewave.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Mar 2028 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated reservation options: cluster sizing & ramp schedule

Markus —

Thanks for the clear options. Quick answers from our side:
- Budget: Q2 ceiling is constrained; we can commit up to $120k/mo starting April, but need to keep runway conservative.
- Compliance: SOC2 is required; data residency in us-east is preferred. On-prem is a future possibility but not in scope for Q2.
- Ramp: prefer monthly cadence with an option to accelerate if model release goes well.

Priya and I want to avoid locking to a 96-GPU slate immediately. Growth Tier sounds closest to our needs, but can you tell us if a 24-GPU midpoint (with 16 min floor) is something you recommend as a compromise? Also: what are the SLA and credits for preemption/maintenance windows?

Forwarding to Priya for any compliance add-ons.

—Daniel
Daniel Gray
Head of AI — PineWave Therapeutics
daniel.gray@pinewave.com

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Mar 2028 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Dedicated reservation options: cluster sizing & ramp schedule

Internal —

Looping you both on PineWave's reply. They have a $120k/mo Q2 cap, prefer growth-level throughput but want to start smaller and keep residency in us-east. Suggestion below:

Recommended approach (internal proposal):
- "Growth-Lite" compromise: 24 GPUs reserved (A100-eq) with a contractual minimum floor of 16 GPUs and monthly checkpointing.
- Ramp schedule: Month 1 = 12 live (warm-start reservations), Month 2 = 16 (operational baseline), Month 3 = 24 (full cap)
- Safety & cost controls: weekend burst windows (+20%) subject to usage caps; automated fallback to hosted instances for occasional spikes to keep committed burn predictable.
- Credits & SLA: include 10% warm-start credit in month 1; 99.5% availability SLA with pro-rata credits for prolonged maintenance (>4h) — confirm legal phrasing with Marissa.
- Compliance & residency: host in us-east single-tenant VPC; SOC2 artifacts ready. Marissa, please confirm if additional language needed on data residency and audit evidence.

Notes for Karthik: please compute the delta between a 32-GPU Growth Tier vs our 24-GPU Growth-Lite (both gross and net after warm-start credits) and flag any infra constraints for a us-east reserved pool. Also include the estimate for failover hosted capacity we would need to guarantee the spike coverage.

Also attaching gputopology.png to help PineWave visualize node mapping for the 24-GPU reserve (shows shard distribution and burst lanes).

Thanks — will prepare a short deck for PineWave once we confirm numbers.

—Markus

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Gray <daniel.gray@pinewave.com>, Priya Reddy <priya.reddy@pinewave.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 06 Mar 2028 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated reservation options: cluster sizing & ramp schedule

Daniel / Priya —

Thanks for the quick feedback. Based on your budget and residency constraints, attached is a consolidated plan and an activation timeline. Key points below:

Consolidated offer: Growth-Lite 24-GPU reservation (16 GPU contractual floor)
- Price: $115k/mo (net of warm-start credit of $8k applied in month 1)
- Activation:
  - Week 0: contract & onboarding (SOW + SOC2 evidence bundle)
  - Month 1: 12 GPUs live (warm-started; engineering onboarding)
  - Month 2: 16 GPUs baseline (operational metrics and cost review)
  - Month 3: 24 GPUs target (full capacity)
- Burst behavior: weekend burst lanes up to +20% for short windows; spikes beyond that auto-failover to hosted capacity (metered).
- SLA & credits: 99.5% availability; standard Redwood credit schedule (pro-rata for outages >4h).
- Data residency: single-tenant VPC in us-east; SOC2 report and access logs provided via secure drive link.

Next steps:
1) Review attached short deck and confirm you want Growth-Lite.
2) I will generate a draft SOW and DocuSign packet (link below) — we can target signature by 2028-03-12 to keep the April activation.
3) Karthik will follow with the exact cost comparison and warm-start credit math.

DocuSign (draft): https://app.redwood.com/docusign/PW-2028-004
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/12345/PW-2028-004

If that works, I'll route the SOW to your legal and copy Marissa for the SOC2 evidence handoff.

Best,
